construct: Gain-of-function pathogenic variants in ACVR1/ALK2 cause dysregulated bone morphogenetic protein signaling and progressive heterotopic endochondral ossification of skeletal muscle, fascia, tendons, and ligaments, often triggered by soft-tissue injury.

adversarial_second_pass.independent_reconstruction: Congenital malformed great toes plus recurrent trauma-triggered heterotopic ossification is fibrodysplasia ossificans progressiva, caused by activating ACVR1/ALK2 signaling in the BMP pathway.
adversarial_second_pass.strongest_distractor_attack: RYR1 defects cause malignant-hyperthermia/congenital-myopathy phenotypes; dystrophin loss causes dystrophinopathy; COL1A1 loss causes osteogenesis imperfecta; FGFR3 gain causes achondroplasia.
adversarial_second_pass.expert_reviewer_reversal: The great-toe malformation plus progressive heterotopic ossification is highly specific for FOP and maps uniquely to ACVR1 among the choices.
